title: Digital Sim Management
definition: The process of handling eSIM profiles during a factory reset on a Samsung device.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of an eSIM as a digital version of a SIM card. When you reset your phone, it will ask you to keep or delete the eSIM. Keeping it means you can still use your phone number and plan, but it won't automatically connect to the network until you allow it.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: During a factory reset on a Samsung device with an eSIM, you're presented with an option to either keep the current eSIM profile or delete it. The eSIM profile is a digital version of a SIM card stored on a secure chip, and it consists of your phone number and plan. Keeping the eSIM profile allows you to reconnect to your carrier's network without needing a new one, but the cellular radio will be dormant until you activate it.
difficulty_levels.expert: The digital SIM management process on a Samsung device during a factory reset is a manifestation of the broader concept of digital identity and privacy. An eSIM profile is a digital representation of a physical SIM card, stored on a secure chip within the device. Keeping the eSIM profile during a factory reset allows for the preservation of digital identity while enabling the user to maintain control over their network connection. This process highlights the importance of understanding and managing digital data within devices, as well as the philosophical implications of privacy and control in a digital world.

extra_fields.insight: The user's ability to keep their eSIM profile during a factory reset allows them to maintain control over their digital identity and network connection, while still providing them with the benefits of a clean, offline device.
